q: Who keeps the signed original of a supplier contract, and for how long?
answer:
The signed original is kept by the **records room**, which the office desk holds. The team that signed the contract does not keep it. When the contract is signed, one of the two originals goes to the records room, and the scan goes into the groupware document store under `contracts/<year>/<vendor>` on the same day. Originals don't leave the building. Borrowing one is logged with the records desk.

It is kept for **10 years** under the retention schedule, based on the Commercial Act. The clock starts when the contract ends, not when it was signed. A contract that ended in 2025 would be kept until 2035. Destruction only happens after a January check by the records desk, and anything under litigation or audit is kept even after its period has run.

For an electronic contract there is no paper original. Keep the PDF together with the signing certificate.

Sources: RouteMind, Procurement → Contract custody (`custody-rule`), and Document retention → Retention period by document (`retention-table`). The procurement and approval areas both route to these documents correctly, so I have no corrections to report.
